why: B states the premise plainly; A's capitalised 'YOUR real work is the material' is more emphatic and wordier.
B compresses the bitter-lesson paragraph, so it has fewer words and a more neutral register.
A skips the added 'curated library' metaphor sentence, so it is shorter.
B cuts the 'Module 5 builds the tools...' forward hint and keeps the closer short.
B's added line asserts the forum 'didn't converge on the first try', which the slide never showed and which may not be true; A has fewer words.
B drops the 'possible problem' closer, so it is shorter and has no unnecessary hedge.
B cuts the 'It works. You watched it work.' line, which congratulates the student and narrates what they did.
B cuts the 'you'll use it everywhere' forward hint and is shorter.
B asks for the guess before revealing the answer, which gives the student a real prediction to make. It is also shorter.
B cuts the closing remark 'The model is good. It is still not 100% deterministic.', a restatement that adds nothing.
B cuts the closer 'Compounding rules files are not tidy', which is a witty aside.
B cuts the forward hint 'That's next module.'
B coins an abstract 'The wall' that the author has rejected as a made-up concept; A says the same thing neutrally.
The author's own call kept the permission framing that lands twice with its why, and B adds 'You don't need to get it right first time', which makes this an experiment.
